question: Annatto seeds and extract is used as adulterant in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**dairy products**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annatto seeds and extracts are commonly used as coloring agents in dairy products, particularly in cheese and butter.
 
• The primary purpose is to give dairy products a consistent, appealing yellow to orange hue.
 
• Annatto is derived from the seeds of the achiote tree, native to tropical regions of the Americas.
 
• It is preferred as a natural coloring agent over synthetic dyes in the food industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Color Additives in Foods**

 
 
• Color additives are used to enhance the appearance of food and beverages, making them more appealing to consumers.
 
• Both natural and synthetic color additives are regulated by food safety authorities to ensure they are safe for consumption.
 
• Examples of natural color additives include beet juice, turmeric, and spirulina extract.
 
 
 
• **Regulation of Food Adulteration**
 
 
• Food adulteration involves the addition of substances to food products to increase quantity and reduce quality.
 
• Food safety authorities, such as the FDA in the United States and FSSAI in India, set strict guidelines to prevent adulteration.
 
• Consumers are encouraged to purchase food products from reputable sources to minimize the risk of adulteration.
 
 
 
• **Health Impacts of Adulterants**
 
 
• Consuming adulterated food can lead to health issues, including allergies, digestive problems, and long-term health risks.
 
• It is crucial to be aware of food labels and ingredient lists to identify potential adulterants.
 
 
 
• **Identification of Natural Food Colors**
 
 
• Natural food colors are often listed on ingredient labels under their specific names or as "natural color."
 
• Consumers seeking to avoid synthetic dyes can look for certifications such as "organic" or "non-GMO," which often use natural colorants.
